lesson.subject: english
lesson.title: Dear Diary
lesson.summary: Write a short diary entry that tells what happened and how you felt.
learning_objectives: Say what a diary is for
Use I, the past tense and feeling words

standards.text: Write about real events, in the correct tense, with capital letters and full stops; say what to write and read it aloud

success_criteria: I can say what a diary is for
I can use I, the past tense and a feeling
lesson.real_life: A Ramadan evening diary, helping Nani cook for Eid, or a rainy walk in the UK.

warm_up.prompt: Which word tells us it already happened?
A sentence starts with a capital letter.
warm_up.explanation: Every sentence starts with a capital.

blocks.markdown: Today's big question: what goes in a diary?
blocks.say: Today we meet the diary. What is it, and what goes inside?

blocks.alt: An open lined notebook with a pen lying on the page and pencils on a wooden desk
blocks.caption: A diary is a notebook where you write about your own days.
blocks.credit: Photo by Clay Banks on Unsplash
blocks.say: This empty notebook is ready for a diary entry. Someone will fill it soon.

blocks.markdown: A **diary** is a personal book about your own days.
blocks.say: A diary is a book about you. You write about your own days.
Famous people kept diaries too. Florence Nightingale wrote about caring for others.
Abdul Sattar Edhi also cared for others in Pakistan. Many people wrote about his kindness.

scenes.caption: Private.
scenes.say: A diary is private. You choose who reads it.

scenes.caption: Any kind of day.
scenes.say: You can write about happy days. You can write about sad days too.

scenes.caption: Remember.
scenes.say: A diary helps you remember. You can read it years later.

question.explanation: A diary is a personal book where you write about your days.

options.text: A personal book about your own days

blocks.markdown: An **entry** starts with the date and Dear Diary.
blocks.say: Each entry starts with the date. Then we write Dear Diary.

scenes.caption: The date.
scenes.say: First, the date. Friday the fifth of May.

scenes.caption: Dear Diary.
scenes.say: Then, Dear Diary. I write to my diary like a friend.

scenes.caption: Past and I.
scenes.say: I write in the past tense. I went, I saw, I felt.

question.prompt: A diary entry starts with the date.
question.hint: Think of the top of the page.

blocks.title: Zainab's Eid diary
blocks.transcript: Today I helped Nani cook for Eid. First, I washed the rice in cold water. Then I stirred the big pot. It smelled delicious. I felt proud. Nani said I helped so much. That night, I opened my diary and wrote the date. Dear Diary, today was wonderful. I felt delighted. I checked my capitals and full stops. Then I read it aloud. I closed my diary. It is my private book.
blocks.caption: Zainab writes about helping Nani cook for Eid.

points: A diary is a personal book
An entry has a date and Dear Diary
We use I, the past tense and feelings
blocks.say: Let us remember. A diary is personal. Entries have a date, I, the past tense and feelings.

blocks.say: A diary also says how you felt. This is what makes it personal.

blocks.markdown: Write a **feeling** sentence for each part.
blocks.say: Add a feeling to each part. I felt happy. I felt proud.

blocks.title: Happy or sad?
blocks.goal: Move each feeling word. Cheerful ones go in Happy. Gloomy ones go in Sad.

blocks.say: Happy is a good word. But there are better ones. Glad, joyful and delighted are happy words.

scenes.caption: Happy words.
scenes.say: Glad and joyful are happy words. Delighted means very happy.

scenes.caption: Sad words.
scenes.say: Gloomy and tearful are sad words. Heartbroken means very sad.

scenes.caption: Worry words.
scenes.say: Nervous and scared are worry words. We feel them before something big.

blocks.say: In the UK, you might write about a rainy walk with family.
